$description: ⑪ The Bottom dock's chrome as a Jx document over the kit: a real `tablist` of the dock's tabs, the button that shuts it, and ONE `tabpanel` for whichever tab is showing. Every tab names that one panel — the dock draws the selected tab's body and no other, so there is exactly one panel element and its `aria-labelledby` follows the selection, which is the same shape `surfaces/git-panel.json` uses for its two sub-tabs. It draws no tab BODY: `panels/bottom-dock.ts` keeps the panel registry, the `when` filter, the badge in each tab's label, the Logic reveal and every tab's `afterRender`, and renders the active record into the one empty `[part="dock-body"]` island this document leaves for it (studio-ui-guidelines.md §9.4).

style.$description: `styles/shell.css`'s four `.bd-*` rules, keyed on `part` and carried here — plus the flex column `#bottom-dock` itself was, because the document root is now the box between the shell cell and the strip and a column that stopped one level up would leave the body unable to scroll. Two rules are DELETED rather than moved: the close button's own padding, radius, hover fill and pointer are `jx-action-button`, and the strip's selected-tab underline is `jx-tab`.

& [part=\"panel\"].$description: The one scrolling region. `min-height: 0` because a flex item's auto minimum is its content, which would push the dock past its own track instead of scrolling inside it.

children.$description: The island, and it stays empty: every tab of this dock is a `PanelRecord` whose `render` returns a lit template, so `panels/bottom-dock.ts` paints here and runs each tab's `afterRender` against this element. It is a slotted child rather than the panel itself because `jx-tab-panel` distributes its own slot.
